policy_facts: The sealed Lovejoin record on the device now also keeps which private session's deposit put a private Bootstrap's or seed's boxes where they are, by that deposit, once its chain's record is gone. Before, it kept this for public accounts only. It is written from the chain record when it goes, or from a seed or Bootstrap entry still open. It is kept while a pool read lists a box there, and 3 hours after. Nothing is sent.

The same record now keeps a list of the leaves it holds after a chain's record goes that one of that chain's mixes made. A box there comes back marked as one a mix moved. It is pruned with the kept leaves and never sent.

No new request anywhere. Bring every box back now, the retired pools' run and Bring one back anyway ask exactly what they asked before. So privacy-policy.md:44 ('asks Koios about the transaction that made it before bringing it back' for a box someone else's mix moved) stays wider than Bring every box back now, as it has been since 1.9.1.

For a box back from Lovejoin, the sealed history notes: a mix moved it; or one of your private sessions deposited it; or a public account deposited it; or nothing the wallet can tell. The last case covers a box someone else put in under your key, which comes back as a box of unknown making, no longer as money received.
Change kept before this release reads its spend's part when the history is read. That is worked out on the device, and nothing new is kept or sent.
needs_wasm_rebuild: The worker now sends origin "change". The current wasm/pkg (20:32) refuses it ('change isn't where a UTxO's money came from'), so until the rebuild every private spend whose candidates include a change-class UTxO throws.

RULES REFINED, FOR R3-docs:
1. Rule 1(d) isn't quite 'everything else'. A box one of the wallet's own chains' mixes made short of its last mixes stays a plain box: Back from Lovejoin alone, no history written, as PRIV-3 has a mix's output and as now. The wallet knows what made it. A public deposit stays box+public:n (PRIV-3, via ties).
2. Rule 1(a) mechanics:
   - A chain's leaf counts as mixed only where one of that chain's mixes made it (its tail's mix included).
   - A leaf kept after the chain's record goes counts as mixed only where this release marked it (Schedule.mixedLeaves).
   - So a leaf 1.9.1 kept with its record gone reads as (d) even if a mix made it: Mint rank 2, not 0. 1.9.1 ranked it as a plain box too.
3. Rule 1(b) mechanics:
   - The Lovejoin record now keeps a seed's or Bootstrap's deposit, private ones included, by deposit (depositors with a session index) once its record goes.
   - It also keeps one an open entry names after 1.9.1 dropped the record.
   - So such a box stays its session's (or account's) money however its mix's count closes.
4. Rule 1(d) when the private balance pays the way back: the class merges with the paying UTxO's history, and merged() names it by reach (for example Received with a payment).
5. Rule 2:
   - Derived only for entries that kept a class (none: Unknown).
   - Kinds: transfer, withdraw, mint (an account mint keeps public:n), remove, lovejoin-launch (private).
   - Never where the kept class names public:<n>, the legacy bare 'public' included.
   - An old Make public to the user's own account (1.9.1 kept no account part) reads as change.
6. Rule 3:
   - Origin 'change' when a class has a change: part and no public:/session:/elsewhere: part. Unknown parts don't stop it. Change naming a session or a spend made elsewhere ranks as a session's, last.
   - Mint: Mixed 0, Received 1, Lovejoin 2, Unknown 3, Change 4, Own 5, Session 6.
   - Fund: the session's own 0, Received 1, Lovejoin|Mixed 2, Unknown 3, Change 4, Own 5, Session 6. Change merges at tier 0, before Own; it was tier 1 as a session's.
   - Pay: Change with Session (1).
   - wasm/README.md (already edited by someone) should say elsewhere: too.
7. Rule 4: the copy keeps the matched history less every box part, its own unknown:<copy> in their place. Example: a copy of a box-paid Seedelf reads change:<mint>+unknown:<copy>, tagged Change and Unknown, ranked as change. It is Unknown alone only when nothing else is left.
8. The note:
   - New kind 'change from an earlier spend' / 'change from N earlier spends'.
   - A box inside a change class is said as that change: no box, no 'undoes'.
   - A box of unknown making counts as one box.
   - The note never says 'This spends  together'.

items.what: privacy.md:169 rewrites the box histories by rule 1. A box is marked mixed only where the wallet knows it's mixed (its own chain's last mix made it, or the server said a mix did). A box a deposit of the user's put in carries what paid for that deposit and is never marked mixed. A box a chain of the user's left short of its last mixes is a box alone. Anything else, someone else's deposit included, is a box tagged Unknown too, which a Seedelf or another session's funding takes after money others paid. Only a box it knows is mixed goes first for a Seedelf or a pool's start; any other goes after money others paid.

items.what: pending.ts. New `writeSent()` (:610-622) writes a payment's Seedelf history. It rethrows WalletLocked only (a lock, or the pin under another phrase) and lets every other error go, including a synchronous throw from activity.sent() before its first await, so a history that can't be written never holds the watch. The three call sites: (1) settleNow's seen branch (:852-868) writes the history before the turn that removes the watch and kept copy and unseals. (2) The sibling in submitWatched (:584-603) writes the history inside the try, before take() unseals the copy written ahead; the old post-take line is deleted, and the existing catch already rethrows a lock. (3) A second sibling, the resend-taken path (:956-967), uses writeSent too, and its catch now rethrows WalletLocked. Before, a lock plus an unlock both landing before the final turn unsealed it with nothing written. A lock at any of these points leaves the sealed copy; the next unlock puts the watch back and its settle writes the entry, which sent() replaces by hash. Doc: architecture.md:318.

policy_facts: l2sign#1 adds one case to what is counted and kept. A site's page leaves its connect question, or its wait for the unlock, unanswered while another of its pages is on its way to ask. If that other page then also leaves before it asks, the site now waits out the back-off and is kept with the declined sites. That is its origin, wait, count and network in memory-only session storage, and its title only in the worker's memory, the same data as any decline. Before this fix such a site was never counted. The 18 November entry's words ("unless another of its pages is asking to connect too: it's kept with the sites you declined") still hold. G8 may add "until that page leaves too"; nothing new is sent or revealed.
